headline: Dropbox Beats Estimates as File Sync Stabilization Continues
body: Dropbox (DBX) reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 68 cents per share, narrowly beating the 67 cents per share anticipated by analysts. Revenue came in at $634.4 million, flat year over year but above expectations. The cloud storage company closed out fiscal 2025 with fourth-quarter revenue above the high end of its guidance, alongside what executives described as better-than-expected stabilization in the company's core file synchronization and sharing (FSS) business. Shares slipped less than 1% in after-hours trading as investors weighed the modest revenue growth against the earnings beat.

headline: Evergy Raises Long-Term Growth Target to 6-8%
body: Evergy (EVRG) established its long-term adjusted earnings per share annual growth target of 6% to 8%+ through 2030, based on the 2026 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint of $4.24. The utility company reported full-year 2025 adjusted EPS of $3.83, missing prior guidance due to weather impacts and weak industrial demand. For 2026, Evergy guided to adjusted EPS of $4.14 to $4.34, assuming normal weather conditions and 3-4% weather-normalized retail sales growth driven by industrial expansion including Panasonic's new facility. Shares rose in pre-market trading as investors welcomed the ambitious long-term growth outlook despite the near-term earnings miss.

headline: Palantir Pulls Back 37% From Highs Amid Valuation Concerns
body: Palantir (PLTR) has plunged 37% from its November highs amid a broader pullback in software stocks and growing worries that the AI leader's valuation may have eclipsed its fundamentals. The stock popped earlier this month after turning in Street-beating fourth-quarter results, but shares have since retreated as analysts question whether current multiples are sustainable. Despite the recent weakness, Mizuho analyst Gregg Moskowitz said the drop has actually created an opportunity, maintaining a buy rating with a 44% upside potential. The stock is down about 27% in 2026 as investors reassess AI valuations across the sector.

headline: Dell Positioned to Benefit From Memory Price Surge
body: Dell Technologies (DELL) is positioned to benefit from surging memory and storage component prices, with reports indicating corporate clients are accelerating hardware purchases to get ahead of projected 15% to 30% price increases in 2026. The PC maker is qualifying memory chips from Chinese manufacturer CXMT for the first time amid fears that DRAM supplies will remain constrained throughout the year. Dell's ISG (Infrastructure Solutions Group) is set to drive combined mid-30% revenue growth in the current quarter, with ISG forecasted to grow in the mid-60s% guided by continued data center modernization and robust Dell IP storage demand. The company's ability to pass higher costs along to enterprise customers demonstrates strong pricing power in the current environment.

headline: Nvidia Blackwell Sales 'Off the Charts' Ahead of Earnings
body: Nvidia (NVDA) shares are in focus ahead of the company's fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings report on February 25, with Oppenheimer and Citi reiterating positive ratings on the AI chip leader. The company reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings of $1.30 per share, with CEO Jensen Huang stating that 'Blackwell sales are off the charts, and cloud GPUs are sold out.' Consensus estimates project 2026 revenue at around $323 billion, propelled by a $500 billion order backlog for its leading Blackwell and Rubin chips. The stock remains a key focus for investors as AI demand continues to drive unprecedented growth in the semiconductor sector.

headline: S&P 500 Advances as Supreme Court Rejects Trump Tariffs
body: The S&P 500 advanced on Friday as traders deemed the Supreme Court's rejection of President Donald Trump's tariff program to be a potential stress on government finances that is unlikely to change the economy's course. Stocks rose while bonds and the dollar slipped, with the Dow up 0.18% and the Nasdaq gaining 0.39%. The market reaction reflects investor relief that the tariff dispute has been resolved, removing a key source of economic uncertainty. However, concerns remain about the broader implications for government spending and fiscal policy in the coming months.
